title: Ocular Mysathenia Gravis Generalization
brief_summary: Secondary ocular myasthenia gravis (OMG) generalization represents a pejorative evolution and no validated generalization prevention strategy exists. The aim of this observational study was to determine the percentage of patients with OMG generalization and identify factors predictive of that pejorative evolution. Data from patients with OMG registered in the Fondation Hospital A. de Rothschild database between January 1990 and January 2017 were collected. Among the 183 patients registered in this database, 151 patients with available informations were analyzed.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

\- Patients with OMG diagnosis and its generalization who consulted between January 1990 to January 2017 at Fondation Hospital Adolphe de Rothschild and registered in the database

Exclusion Criteria:

\- OMG differential diagnoses
study_population: Patients with OMG diagnosis and its generalization who consulted between January 1990 to January 2017 at Fondation Hospital Adolphe de Rothschild and registered in the database
